Hi Evan — appreciate the clarity. Short answer up front: for CardioHealth’s constraints (EU residency requirement + 120ms p95 ingest) we recommend Dedicated for the initial launch, with a fallback hosted routing policy for burst protection. Below is the recommended evaluation and close timeline.

Recommended path (summary):
- Mode: Dedicated (EU region, primary eu-west-1 cluster)
- Why: Dedicated gives you single-tenant GPU pools, predictable throughput to meet 120ms p95 for edge-to-model hops, and isolation that makes procurement/compliance clearance simpler than our shared hosted tier.
- Fallback: Configure smart routing to hosted EU nodes for non-sensitive traffic or overload events during first 3 months.

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) PO & procurement kickoff (Day 0–7): procurement sends initial ASN and SOW requests — we provide SOC2 evidence and security questionnaire answers (attached).
2) Dedicated provisioning & connectivity (Day 7–21): account team reserves Dedicated capacity in eu-west; networking team validates peering/VPN.
3) PoC (Day 21–35): 2-week PoC with your test payloads; perf targets: p95 < 140ms in week 1, <120ms in week 2.
4) Go/no-go & cutover plan (Day 35–42): sign-off from compliance + Prod readiness checklist complete.

If you want to keep procurement timelines short, we can parallelize the questionnaire and capacity reservation. I’ve attached a MAP XLSX with milestones and ownership.

Available for a 1pm CET call tomorrow — I’ll add Karthik (solutions) if we take that slot.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether procurement prefers Dedicated-only or wants Hosted fallback in the SOW.
- Share any additional compliance artifacts we should pre-populate.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: internal — CardioHealth hosting recommendation and perf assumptions

Folks — quick internal note to capture engineering constraints and recommended knobs if we go Dedicated for CardioHealth. Copying ticket links in comments.

Key perf assumptions:
- Estimated tokens/month (initial): 5M (increased to 8–10M after Q3 if expansion).
- Model: 13B encoder-decoder variant; latency budget depends on sequence-length, plan for average 64 tokens request payload.
- Target: p95 < 120ms from EU ingress to token emission; this implies colocated Dedicated GPUs (A10x or H100 fractional) with batch size tuning and KV cache warm-up.

Operational recommendations:
- Capacity: reserve 2x baseline nodes (redundancy + headroom for bursts) with autoscale threshold at 70% sustained util.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for known prompt templates (CardioHealth standard prompts) to shave ~15–25ms per request.
- Quantization: provide a quantized variant for Dedicated to meet cost targets; Redwood Optimize will output quantizationprofile_v2 for workload.
- Fallback routing: configure Hosted EU pool with automatic fallback during capacity pressure; ensure data routing flag marks any PII-sensitive requests as restricted to Dedicated only.

Procurement/security notes to include for Olga’s email: SOC2 report location, encryption-at-rest KMS details, retention policy (30 days ephemeral cache, logs retained 90 days with audit export).

I’ll attach a short perf-run checklist to the MAP doc before handing back to you.

—Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
